summary.name: Smederee
summary.one_liner: Smederee is a self-hosted, frugal software forge that hosts Darcs version-control repositories and lets people build software together.
use_cases: Host Darcs repositories on your own server
Collaborate on software projects with a self-hosted forge
Run a small private or community code hosting service
summary.what_it_does: Smederee is a platform for hosting Darcs version-control repositories and supporting collaborative software development. The page describes repositories accessed over SSH (read-only and read-write clone URLs) and a separate tickets component that integrates with the hub. It is a Scala application requiring Java 17+, PostgreSQL 13+ with the DBMS time zone set to Etc/UTC, and Darcs, with optional colordiff and tokei. Setup is done by building a tarball with sbt, writing an application.conf (including a required cookie-secret of at least 64 alphanumeric characters), and running it behind a reverse proxy such as nginx that handles HTTPS. The page also covers SSH client configuration with a custom port and per-schema database permissions.
notable: Built on the Darcs version control system instead of Git
Hub and tickets components can run under one domain or separate subdomains
Requires a reverse proxy for HTTPS; ships a tarball built with sbt
Licensed under EUPL 1.2 or later (listing says AGPL-3.0)
caveats: Currently only the repository owner can use it via SSH
SSH cloning needs an RSA key (ed25519 support is experimental) and a custom port
Requires PostgreSQL, Java 17+, and a correctly configured database time zone
